I used to work at a lab. Results were run 24 hours a day. If one of the lab techs resulted something that was dangerously out of range for any given patient, it was the responsibility of the laboratory to contact the ordering physician and let them know. These results were considered "critical" and the patient could suffer serious consequences or die if not looked after immediately. It didn't matter if it was 2AM or 2PM, as soon as a result was found to be critical, the physician was called, and the physician would usually call the patient and tell them to go to the ER. We didn't result blood pressure (this has to be done on-site, usually in a doctor's office) but if the patient's bloodwork came back with say, extremely high glucose (>30mmol/L) which could cause seizures, temporary blindness, etc. we would have to call the doctor, who usually called the patient. So the doctor is just doing his job. You have to have some pretty messed up (read: emergency) results for the doctor to call you that late at night though.
